title: Studio MCP's simulated mouse leaves the camera Fixed
observation: In a Studio play session, any Studio MCP user_mouse_input action (a plain x/y move as well as an instance_path click) switched workspace.CurrentCamera.CameraType from Custom to Fixed, and it stayed Fixed. When the game then teleported the character (raid start onto a flying ship, 5,000 studs away) the camera stayed behind at the old place, which looked exactly like a game bug. A listener on the camera's CameraType showed the change at the moment of the mouse action; no game code sets Fixed (searched), and setting Custom from a client execute_luau restored a following camera at once. The tool's x/y coordinates were also 58 px above the game's own mouse and viewport coordinates (the GUI inset).
recommendation: After any simulated mouse action in a Studio playtest, reset the camera (CameraType = Custom) from a client execute_luau before judging what the camera shows, and log CameraType changes before reporting a camera bug. Convert WorldToViewportPoint y to the tool's coordinates by subtracting the GUI inset, or click buttons by instance_path.
applies_when: Playtesting a Roblox game through Studio MCP input tools
Judging camera behaviour, or anything after a teleport, in a session that used the simulated mouse
limits: One Windows PC, Studio in October 2026, a 1346 x 640 play viewport
Whether the tool restores the camera later on its own was not established; real mice are unaffected

evidence.detail: Section 12, last bullet; the camera log read '5.3:Custom ... 9.4:Fixed' around a simulated click, and 'Fixed' again after a plain x/y move.
